guarantees.claim: idle_d is computed with a priority: asserted low when reg_hash_start_i or reg_hash_continue_i is high; otherwise high if FSM is in StIdle; otherwise high if txcnt_eq_blksz and reg_hash_stop_d are both true; otherwise it holds the previous idle_q value.
idle_o is always driven directly by idle_d.

assumptions.claim: idle_q is a registered, delayed version of idle_d from the previous clock cycle, providing stable fallback.
assumptions.cond: when idle_d depends on idle_q for hold
assumptions.risk: If idle_q is not a delayed copy, combinational feedback on idle_d can cause oscillation or glitches on idle_o, misleading downstream about core idle status.

uncertain_points.claim: idle_q must be proven to be a registered version of idle_d outside this chunk; otherwise a combinational loop exists.
uncertain_points.risk: Unstable idle_o could break handshake protocols or cause premature pipeline advance.

uncertain_points.claim: The combo of txcnt_eq_blksz and reg_hash_stop_d may be a short pulse or asynchronous, causing idle_d to prematurely assert idle_o before actual completion of stop processing.
uncertain_points.risk: Core could be marked idle while still finalizing a block, leading to data corruption or handshake race.

uncertain_points.claim: If reg_hash_start_i and reg_hash_continue_i are both asserted, the combinatorial OR forces idle_d low regardless of other conditions; it is unclear if this combination is legal and intended to override a concurrent stop.
uncertain_points.risk: Unexpected FSM behavior or ignored stop command could lead to protocol mismatch.
